main.label: This site's assumptions
main.note: Imaging growth per person starts near 1.2%/yr.

ai_skeptic.label: AI-skeptical
ai_skeptic.note: Stall/Trend/Fast/Transformative weights 30/55/12/3%, nearer forecasting panels, which put far lower odds on transformative AI than AI-lab leaders.

ai_bullish.label: AI-bullish
ai_bullish.note: Stall/Trend/Fast/Transformative weights 5/35/30/30%, nearer AI-lab leaders and AI 2027 (a widely read scenario of very fast AI progress).

imaging_restraint.label: Imaging restraint
imaging_restraint.note: Imaging per person grows ~0.4%/yr: close to claims-based 2018-22 trends, plus payer and Medicare cost pressure (v1.5 assumed 0.6%/yr).

imaging_growth.label: Imaging growth
imaging_growth.note: Imaging per person grows ~1.8%/yr: what the history reconstruction implies for 2022-2026, near recent CT growth.

residency_slows.label: Residency growth slows
residency_slows.note: Positions grow only ~0.5%/yr as Medicare GME caps bind.

residency_growth.label: Residency growth continues
residency_growth.note: Residency positions keep growing ~1.9%/yr, the 2010-2025 pace.

favorable.label: Lowest-risk combination: AI-skeptical + imaging growth
favorable.note: Combines the two single changes that lower oversupply risk most.

unfavorable.label: Highest-risk combination: AI-bullish + imaging restraint
unfavorable.note: Combines the two single changes that raise oversupply risk most.

no_signoff.label: No radiologist on AI-first reads
no_signoff.detail: No audit or sign-off time at all on AI-first reads

unordered.label: Tiers automated in any order
unordered.detail: Complex exams may be automated before simple ones

open_demand.label: Much more new imaging
open_demand.detail: 3× as many new AI-enabled imaging uses and 2× the new radiologist tasks

payer_pushback.label: Stronger payer pushback
payer_pushback.detail: Payers' AI blocks twice as many scans; twice as many reads shift to other doctors

uncapped_new_uses.label: New uses not capped by scanners
uncapped_new_uses.detail: New uses such as screening existing scans are not limited by scanner capacity

tai_gated.label: Transformative boost waits for regulation
tai_gated.detail: Transformative AI's extra time savings must also wait for regulation and adoption

no_adjustment.label: No market adjustment (other v1.6 inputs kept)
no_adjustment.detail: Market adjustment removed (v1.5's design) but v1.6's other inputs kept; those were calibrated with the adjustment on

shortage_only.label: Surpluses not absorbed
shortage_only.detail: The market absorbs shortages as fitted but not surpluses: work does not flow back to radiologists

adj_cap15.label: Adjustment limit at most 15%
adj_cap15.detail: Adjustment limit capped at 15% of demand, the largest gap seen in 1995-2026

adj_wide.label: Larger adjustment (limit up to 50%)
adj_wide.detail: Adjustment speed and limit as in the fit with wider priors (limit up to 50% of demand)

adj_start.label: Adjustment starts from its reconstructed 2026 state
adj_start.detail: The adjustment starts from the reconstruction's 2026 state instead of zero (less room to absorb a surplus if work already moved to radiologists)

assistive_only.label: Assistive AI only
assistive_only.detail: AI helps radiologists read but never reads first

no_ai.label: No further radiology AI
no_ai.detail: Radiology AI frozen at its 2026 level (other diagnostics such as AI-ECG still displace some imaging)

tier1_2022.label: Normal-X-ray AI capable since 2022
tier1_2022.detail: Tier-1 capability centred on 2022 (EU approval) instead of 2025. If AI could do this since 2022 and the FDA still has not approved it, regulation must be slow, so fewer fast-AI futures fit the facts

no_shortage_today.label: Little or no shortage today
no_shortage_today.detail: Today's supply ÷ demand anywhere from 0.95 to 1.03 (main model: full range 0.88-0.99)
